entries.title: Proverbs 22:1
segments: Our comfort and usefulness depend on our character, rather than on our outward possessions.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:2
segments:
Meet together; come into contact in various relations of life. 
 
  The Lord is the maker of them all; he is their common Lord, has placed them together in this world, and will call them to an account for their treatment of each other.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:3
segments: In the gospel of his Son, God has provided a refuge from the evil that is coming upon all sinners.  The highest wisdom of men is to hide themselves in this refuge; to neglect it, is their folly and ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:5
segments: The way of those who oppose themselves to God's government must be filled with "thorns and snares."  It is in the path of duty that we find comfort and safety.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:6
segments: In committing to parents the training of their children, God has, in a very important sense, committed to them the formation of their future character, and he will hold them responsible for the influence they exert.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:7
segments: To contract debts beyond our ability to pay, is to rob ourselves of that manly independence which belongs to the righteous man's character, and to expose ourselves to innumerable temptations as well as annoyances.  For this reason, as well as from regard to our own reputation and the rights of others, it is a cardinal Christian virtue to "owe no man any thing, but to love one another."

entries.title: Proverbs 22:8
segments:
Vanity; disappointment and misery. 
 
  The rod of his anger; the rod wherewith he smote his fellow-men in anger. 
 
They who occupy themselves with devising mischief to others, are preparing for themselves a harvest of shame and trouble.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:11
segments: The grace of his lips; his pleasant and well-timed words.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:12
segments: Preserve knowledge; watch over and protect knowledge, by protecting those who possess it and use it for the good of their fellow-men.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:13
segments: The slothful exaggerate the difficulties that lie in the way of duty.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:14
segments: Mouth of strange women; their "much fair speech,"

. 
 
  Abhorred of the Lord; because he turns aside from the right way.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:16
segments: Giveth to the rich; from selfish motives, to purchase their favor.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:17
segments: Here begins another division of the book, extending to the end of the twenty-fourth chapter.  It has a general resemblance to the first nine chapters.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:19
segments: Made known; that is, these words.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:20
segments: In counsels and knowledge; containing counsels and words of knowledge.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:21
segments: To them that send unto thee; to ask counsel of thee.  Or, "To those that send thee;" tht is, mayest make a true report to them of the business intrusted to thee.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:22
segments: In the gate; where courts were anciently held, and public business was transacted.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:23
segments: The more destitute one is of human protection, the greater is the guilt and the danger of wronging him; the Lord is the patron of the defenceless, and will avenge the injuries done to them.

entries.title: Proverbs 22:29
segments: Diligence in business leads to preferment and honor.
